committed: Before js/kernels/atmospheres/, the validation tool, the oracle's results and the tests existed. The bounds are Prompt 199's (tests/fixtures/atmospheres-gate-i/thresholds.json, verdict B, D-R10-75), carried over unchanged; no bound is reset here. The escape checks J1 to J4 are not part of this file: verdict B builds Prompt 200 without the escape panel and the escape data are unmeasured.

models.equilibrium: T_eq = [(1 - A) S f / sigma]^(1/4), A the Bond albedo, f = 2/3 - 5 eps / 12 for a redistribution efficiency eps in [0, 1] (1/4 for uniform redistribution; Cowan and Agol 2011). Not a surface temperature.
models.oneLayer: One isothermal layer, transparent to sunlight, emissivity eps_L in [0, 1]: T_s = T_e [2 / (2 - eps_L)]^(1/4), T_layer = T_s / 2^(1/4); the surface cannot exceed 2^(1/4) T_e, so the model has no solution above that ratio.
models.grey: Grey radiative equilibrium, Eddington closure: T^4(tau) = (3/4) T_e^4 (tau + 2/3), tau from the top; ground T_g^4 = T_e^4 (1 + 3 tau_s / 4). A different model from the one layer; its optical depth is not the one layer's emissivity.
models.scaleHeight: H = k T / (mu m_u g): isothermal, hydrostatic, constant gravity, well mixed.

anchors.note: Published numbers typed from the cited publications and not re-read against them in the session that wrote them (Prompt 199 recorded the same). Their tolerances are wide enough that a one-digit slip would not change a status; a reader with the sources must check them before any is called verified.

Jupiter.source: Hanel et al. 1981, J. Geophys. Res. 86, 8705

Neptune.source: Pearl and Conrath 1991, J. Geophys. Res. 96, 18921

seed.stream: js/rng.js mulberry32, the seed of the gate that fixed these counts

tiers.a: the closed forms, their limits, monotonicity and the anchors (checks a1 to a4, a6, s1, s2)
tiers.b: an independent oracle in numpy and scipy (no Gravitas code): the closed forms to 1e-12, the grey two-stream moment equations by solve_ivp at three pinned optical depths, the exact grey solution by the Milne equation (checks a1, a3, a4, b1, b2, s1)
tiers.c: not applicable: the kernel fits no uncertainty and returns none
tiers.d: an optical depth or any input outside a model's domain is refused with the reason and no number (check d1)

a1.equilibrium.what: equilibrium temperature against the oracle on 2,000 seeded (flux, Bond albedo, redistribution) points

a2.anchors.what: Venus, Earth and Mars emission temperatures against the textbook 227, 255 and 210 K; Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune against the temperature implied by the published effective temperature and emitted-to-absorbed power ratio; HD 209458 b (A = 0, full redistribution) inside 1,400 to 1,500 K and equal to the transit lesson's own formula

a3.onelayer.what: one-layer surface and layer temperature against the oracle's linear solve of the two balance equations on 1,000 seeded points; eps = 0 gives T_e, eps = 1 gives 2^(1/4) T_e; monotone in eps

a4.grey.what: grey profile and ground against the oracle's closed forms (1,000 points) and against a numerical solution of the two-stream moment equations for 60 surface optical depths from 0.01 to 200

a6.report.what: for Venus, Earth and Mars the one-layer emissivity and the grey optical depth that reproduce the measured surface temperature, each result naming its model; the one-layer model refuses for Venus (ratio above 2^(1/4)); the values are reported and never asserted against a published optical depth

b1.eddington.what: the Eddington profile against the exact grey solution (the Milne equation solved by an independent scipy program with its own self-test: q(0) = 0.5774 and q(infinity) = 0.7104 to 1 percent): relative difference in temperature at most 4.0 percent at every depth from 0 to 100, the model's stated error, shown and not minimised

b2.pinnedProfiles.what: the grey profile at three surface optical depths (0.87, 10 and 141.5: the Earth-like and Venus-like fits and one between) against the pinned two-stream solution at tau = 0, tau_s / 3 and tau_s: relative difference in T at most 1e-6

c.uncertainty.what: not applicable: no fitted uncertainty is returned; stated, not run

d1.refusals.what: 24 hostile inputs each refuse with a named reason and no number (albedo, emissivity and redistribution outside [0, 1]; non-positive, infinite or NaN flux; an optical depth below 0, infinite or NaN; non-positive temperature, mean molecular weight or gravity; a ratio the model cannot reach); every result names its model and what it leaves out (at least three assumptions)

s1.scale.what: scale height against the oracle (astropy constants) on 1,000 seeded points, and as an e-folding length: a numerically integrated isothermal hydrostatic column has pressure ratio e at height H

s2.anchors.what: scale heights at 737, 288 and 210 K and the application's gravities and mean molecular weights against the fact-sheet 15.9, 8.5 and 11.1 km

p1.pack.what: the planetary parameter pack: six bodies, each parameter carrying its source and the flag that it was typed and not re-read; albedos in [0, 1]; no exobase or escape field; the measured-temperature comparison labels the difference and says that a giant planet has no surface

b3.hopfApproximation.what: added for the instruments (Prompt 200 follow-up), before it was measured: the exact grey curve the greenhouse instrument draws uses the Hopf function q(tau) = 0.7104 - 0.1331 exp(-3.4488 tau) in T^4 = (3/4) T_e^4 (tau + q(tau)); against the pinned Milne solution at the 401 depths of b1 its temperature differs by at most 0.5 percent, and q(0) is within 0.1 percent of 1/sqrt(3)

p2.lessonNumbers.what: added for the lessons, before they were written: every number a step of 'Why Venus Is Hot' and 'Two Greenhouse Models' states is recomputed from the kernel and the pack in tests/atmosphereLessons.test.js, each to the precision the step states it
